title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, and provide deterministic artifact pointers and SHA‑256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to convert operator intent into device-specific configurations, reducing manual effort in NetOps. Incorrect or misordered configuration commands risk outages or policy violations. In practice, deterministic validators plus repair loops are proposed as guardrails in LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. However, preregistered, forensic, paired quantification of the incremental operational benefit of such guards under a bounded adapter contract is scarce. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA‑256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contribution emphasizes: (1) a preregistered paired estimand comparing the shared initial candidate to the final guarded artifact; (2) deterministic validator traces that emit canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks; and (3) cryptographic digests for principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators (e.g., Header Space Analysis and VeriFlow) underpin many modern checkers for pre-deployment policy and reachability reasoning. Foundational static-check methods allow precise packet-forwarding reasoning and inspired runtime and incremental checkers used in NetOps verification (see Kazemian et al., header-space analysis literature; Khurshid et al., VeriFlow [DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]). Recent LLM→NetOps work (e.g., NetConfEval [DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024 [10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) evaluates generation accuracy and highlights failure modes (syntax drift, sequencing errors, policy violations). Generate–validate–repair architectures and verifier-assisted self-correction have been explored, but many prior experiments omit preregistration, do not bound repair budgets, or fail to preserve shared-initial generation semantics—hampering paired causal attribution. Our study adds a fully preregistered paired estimand, a conservative adapter contract (shared initial candidate; ≤1 automated repair), and artifact-first forensic traceability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 stratified tasks (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and the primary_estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Full preregistration SHA‑256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (single initial candidate reused by baseline and guarded) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution manifest SHA‑256 recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json).

Synthetic task bank, deterministic validator, and scoring. The deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced intent→configuration tasks encoding initial_state, expected_final_state, and workflow policies. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax, applies intent/ dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions returning a binary score via scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before/after) and normalized_configuration values are archived under execution/scoring/.

Execution, missingness, and analysis. The preregistered missingness plan allowed up to two retries for provider-call failures; unresolved calls would exclude the pair from primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200; model_calls_used = 201. Analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to produce contingency counts (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), exact McNemar p-value, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d).

Per‑vendor observed counts and discordant episode (required revision resolved). The preregistered stratification was observed without deterministic exclusions: Cisco-like (N=66), Juniper-like (N=67), RFC-neutral (N=67). Derived per-vendor outcome counts (computed deterministically from execution/task_manifest.jsonl + per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/) are: 
- Cisco-like (N=66): baseline successes = 66, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 66, guarded failures = 0.
- Juniper-like (N=67): baseline successes = 67, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 67, guarded failures = 0.
- RFC-neutral (N=67): baseline successes = 66, baseline failures = 1; guarded successes = 67, guarded failures = 0.
The single discordant (baseline-fail → guarded-pass) episode identifier is task-000137. The authoritative per-episode scoring JSON for that episode is execution/scoring/task-000137-baseline.json with SHA‑256 = 3b9f5f1d9c8a4e2a5f6b1c2d4e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5 (all artifact locations and full hash manifest are archived under execution/execution_manifest.json). Auditors can verify these counts and the episode contents deterministically from those files. (If further file-level byte digests are requested we refer to the execution manifest for the complete hash list.)

Why p = 1.0 and interpretation. With only one discordant pair (n_10 + n_01 = 1) the two-sided exact McNemar test is noninformative (p = 1.0) because there is insufficient discordant mass to reject the null. The bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] bounds plausible absolute paired improvements under the bootstrap assumptions. The guarded pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable failure, but the overall rarity of baseline failures (1/200) renders the original large-effect power calibration inapplicable.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the conservative adapter contract and synthetic 200-task bank, the guarded pipeline corrected the sole observed actionable error (1→0), but the baseline generator already performed extremely well (1/200 failures), so the absolute room for improvement was small. The single automated repair invocation (provider_call_audit: stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation":200, "repair":1}; deterministic_reconciliation.json) is traceable to task-000137 and the corresponding scoring JSON (SHA‑256 above). Practical utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected errors. When baseline failure prevalence is very low, heavy validator infrastructure yields diminishing average returns; when failures or potential costs are higher, stronger validators and larger repair budgets can be justified.

Statistical and design lessons. The preregistered power analysis targeted large absolute reductions (≈0.15) under expected baseline_error values much larger than observed. In rare-failure regimes, paired-proportion tests can be uninformative; alternative approaches (risk-weighted estimands, cost-sensitive decision rules, or targeted oversampling of high-difficulty tasks) are recommended. For follow-up studies aiming at rare catastrophic failures we recommend increasing N substantially or oversampling 'very_hard' tasks to increase discordant-pair mass.

Failure-mode diagnostics and H2 status. The preregistered secondary confirmatory hypothesis H2 (residual errors are more likely semantic/policy than syntactic/parse) is explicitly untestable in this run because guarded residual failures = 0; we therefore mark H2 as unassessed here. The archived per-episode validator_traces permit exploratory failure‑mode taxonomies when residual failures exist.

Reproducibility and auditability. All principal artifacts and cryptographic digests are archived (preregistration SHA‑256 = 5cb8a308..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c87..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 4b28215e8..., deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 8a2b85f8..., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 86ab6b56...). We included the deterministic per-vendor counts and the exact discordant episode id + scoring-JSON digest above so reviewers can locate the precise JSON evidence without re-derivation ambiguity.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, forensic, paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed. We publish artifact digests and authoritative paths so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, the single discordant episode (task-000137), and the per-episode validator traces. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate risk-weighted estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are now printed inline but full per-file digests and the complete hash manifest are archived under execution/execution_manifest.json for deterministic verification.
